raw_case_text:
We present here the case of a 46-old man, a stockbreeder from the Central Bosnia Canton who was treated for PV endocarditis due to Brucella during 2007. In 1998, he underwent an aortic and mitral mechanical valve replacement surgery due to juvenile rheumatic fever. He was doing well, being work-engaged until 2006, when he started to complain about night sweating, chills, exhaustion, dyspnea, palpitations and chest oppression. At that time he did not measure his body temperature. After more than one year of over repeated hospitalizations at the Department of Internal Medicine of Regional Hospital due to "symptoms of heart failure", he was referred to the Clinic for Infectious Diseases, Clinical Center of Sarajevo University. Upon confirmation of the disease, based on positive blood cultures (B.melitensis) taken during everyday subfebrile temperatures, formerly unrecognized, and on transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) indicative of endocarditis, the patient was transferred to Clinic for Infectious Diseases in Sarajevo.
Upon admission, he had cardiac and extra-cardiac manifestations of endocarditis (systolic-diastolic murmur with absolute arrhythmia, splinter haemorrhages, and laboratory criteria for glomerulonephritis) and symptoms of severe heart failure (class III/IV) according to the New York Heart Association (NYHA) criteria. Standard chest radiography and abdominal ultrasound revealed cardiomegaly, hepatosplenomegaly and stasis in the lungs and liver. Coxiella burnetii coinfection was confirmed by ELISA (enzyme linked immunosorbent assey) test (IgG F2+, IgG F1+, IgA F1+).
Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) confirmed the presence of restenosis, multiple mobile vegetations (5-8 mm) attached to mitral and aortic valve (MV, AV) and signs of severe pulmonary hypertension. He did not respond to quadruple antimicrobial and cardiac therapy. A follow-up TEE performed at the end of the third therapeutic week confirmed progression of the disease: "...persistent multiple mobile vegetations at both valves 7-10 mm, left atrial thrombus 7x10 mm...".

subjective.chief_complaint: A 46-year-old male stockbreeder with prosthetic aortic and mitral valves presented with chronic night sweats, chills, exhaustion, dyspnea, palpitations, and chest oppression.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient underwent mechanical aortic and mitral valve replacements in 1998 for juvenile rheumatic fever. He remained functional until 2006, when he insidiously developed night sweats, chills, exhaustion, dyspnea, palpitations, and chest oppression. He endured over one year of repeated hospitalizations at a regional internal medicine department for refractory heart failure before daily subfebrile temperatures were identified and blood cultures obtained, leading to referral to the university infectious disease clinic.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of juvenile rheumatic fever; status-post mechanical aortic and mitral valve replacement surgery in 1998. Occupation: stockbreeder from Central Bosnia Canton. Prior antibiotic exposure not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Night sweats, chills, exhaustion, dyspnea, palpitations, chest oppression; symptoms of NYHA class III/IV heart failure. Home medications: cardiac and anticoagulation medications (details not documented). Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: subfebrile daily body temperatures. Cardiovascular: systolic-diastolic murmurs with absolute arrhythmia over prosthetic valves; peripheral stasis signs including splinter hemorrhages. Abdomen: hepatosplenomegaly. Pulmonary: lung stasis/crackles. Functional status: NYHA class III/IV heart failure.
objective.routine_investigations: Standard chest radiography: cardiomegaly and pulmonary venous stasis. Abdominal ultrasonography: hepatosplenomegaly and hepatic stasis. Laboratory tests: fulfilled laboratory criteria for glomerulonephritis (specific values not documented). Serology: Coxiella burnetii coinfection confirmed by ELISA (IgG Phase 2 positive, IgG Phase 1 positive, IgA Phase 1 positive).
objective.advanced_workup: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE): findings indicative of infective endocarditis. Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE): mechanical valve restenosis, multiple mobile vegetations (5-8 mm) attached to prosthetic mitral and aortic valves, and signs of severe pulmonary hypertension; follow-up TEE at end of week 3 showed disease progression with persistent multiple mobile vegetations (7-10 mm) on both valves and a left atrial thrombus measuring 7 x 10 mm.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Brucella prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) involving mechanical aortic and mitral valves, complicated by Coxiella burnetii (Q fever) coinfection, prosthetic valve restenosis, severe pulmonary hypertension, left atrial thrombus, NYHA class III/IV heart failure, and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis.
Confirmation: Blood cultures grew Brucella melitensis taken during daily subfebrile episodes; TTE and TEE demonstrated multiple prosthetic valve vegetations; Coxiella burnetii coinfection confirmed by ELISA (IgG Phase 2+, IgG Phase 1+, IgA Phase 1+).
Differentials ruled out: Isolated non-infectious prosthetic valve dysfunction / heart failure ruled out by positive microbiological cultures and echocardiographic vegetations.
Treatment & Outcome: Managed with quadruple antimicrobial therapy (including standard anti-brucellar agents) and intensive medical heart failure therapy. Patient failed to respond clinically and echocardiographically, with week 3 TEE demonstrating enlarging vegetations (7-10 mm) and an intracardiac thrombus.
